assessment_summary: The statement is false. Triangle-free graphs can have arbitrarily large chromatic numbers, as demonstrated by Mycielski's construction. For instance, applying the Mycielskian to the Grötzsch graph (which is triangle-free and 4-chromatic) produces a triangle-free graph with a chromatic number of 5. Such a graph is not 4-colourable. Therefore, any attempt to prove this statement for all triangle-free graphs will inherently fail.
counterexample: The Mycielskian of the Grötzsch graph is a triangle-free graph with chromatic number 5.
